name: Phaser + chorus pad from pure waves: triangle and sine unison stacks on one note in three octaves, slow filter-envelope opening, triplet-synced phaser, deep feedback chorus, notch the phaser whistle, dark church-style reverb
goal: Make a soft trance/ambient background pad whose movement comes almost entirely from a phaser and a feedback chorus rather than modulation: soft triangle and sine unison stacks play the same note in three octaves, a slow filter envelope opens the tone as notes hold, and the space comes from a dark, low-cut convolution-style reverb. Delta vs the phaser cluster: pure-wave (triangle/sine) source, phaser + chorus in series as the only motion, and cutting the resonant 'whistle' the phaser creates.
prerequisites: Any synth with 2 oscillators (triangle, sine), unison, 24 dB low-pass and a mod envelope
Phaser and chorus effects (or all-pass chain + modulated short delay)
Reverb with EQ on the return (convolution or algorithmic hall)

inputs.name: progression
inputs.description: Chord roots or the bass progression to follow

outputs.name: phasing_pad
outputs.description: Soft, slowly opening pad with phaser/chorus movement that sits behind the mix

constraints: Original synthesis/processing recipe; not affiliated with any vendor named in the source. Recreate in browser/Web Audio (Polyrhythm Studio) or any DAW/synth with comparable modules; no presets, banks, impulse responses or samples copied.
Unison detune stays small and static (no random pitch); movement comes from phaser and chorus only.
Prefer triangle/sine sources for this pad; they are the softest and leave room for effects to add motion.
Keep the pad in the background: no extra modulation, simple levels.
Drums early (Matt's taste): if the track has drums, the kick/drum loop enters by about count 8 (roughly 10-12 s), with only the pad before that.

steps.action: Write the clip as the same note in three octaves (e.g. B0, B1, B2) following the progression of the bass.

Osc 1: triangle, 6 unison voices, small static detune, wide stereo, centre pan, retrigger on. Osc 2: sine, 8 unison voices, slightly more detune, phase offset (~85 degrees), retrigger on. Raise polyphony since several notes play.
Amp envelope: back the attack off so each note fades in slowly; keep sustain high.

24 dB/oct low-pass with a mod envelope on cutoff: cutoff a little below full (about 70% of range), slow envelope attack (about 65% of its range) and medium sustain (about 50%), so the filter opens gradually while notes hold.
steps.expect: Tone warms and brightens slowly during each note

steps.action: Phaser: spread at maximum, left/right offset centred, width about half, default feedback, dry/wet about 38-40%, LFO rate tempo-synced slightly slower than 1/8 (the source uses a 4/1-triplet style setting).
Chorus after the phaser: delay about 4 ms, rate about 0.25 Hz, depth about 60%, feedback on (chorus feeds back into itself), width maximum, dry/wet about 40%.
Solo the pad and listen for a resonant whistle the phaser creates; cut that band with a narrow, deep EQ notch.

Reverb as an insert or send at about 35% wet: slow, large hall/church-type space, pre-delay about 10 ms, size and decay at maximum; on the reverb's EQ cut everything below 150 Hz and roll the highs off around 4.5 kHz. Add a light compressor after it (shorter release) to bring the reverb up.
steps.expect: Rich, dark space that does not muddy the bass

steps.action: Sidechain-compress the pad to the kick for gentle pump and automate the pad filter so it comes in and out across sections.
steps.expect: Pad breathes with the kick and the arrangement

verification: The pad is the same note in three octaves following the bass roots.
Only phaser and chorus move the sound; pitch is steady.
Filter opens audibly over each held note.
No resonant whistle peak remains after the notch.
Reverb return has nothing below about 150 Hz.
